subject: HealthGrid DPA: operationalizing training-opt-out, regional export lanes, and escrow fallback
messages:
From: Sophia Ramos <sophia.ramos@healthgrid.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@healthgrid.com, m.torres@healthgrid.com
Date: 2028-04-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on DPA redline (training opt-out + export lanes)

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the DPA redline. A couple of follow-ups from our legal and procurement teams as we prepare for signatures:

- We need confirmation that HealthGrid data will not be used to improve or retrain models (no-training) — the redline references an "exclusion" but we need an operational description of how that's enforced (subprocessors, logs, retention).
- Can you outline the operational path if onshore KMS is required for our EU/US residency: do you offer onshore KMS + SFTP export lanes, or is there an escrow fallback we can rely on?
- Who are the subprocessors involved in inference and caching (we see a reference to caching infra) and what proof/attestation will you provide?

Procurement is also asking for a rough delta in pricing for the onshore/residency option vs hosted. We attached our current redline (HealthGrid_DPA_redline_v3.pdf).

Would like to sync early next week — available Mon/Tue afternoon PT.

Best,
Sophia Ramos
Head of Privacy & Compliance
HealthGrid

Attachment: HealthGrid_DPA_redline_v3.pdf

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-20T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redline (training opt-out + export lanes)

Sophia — thanks for the clear note and the redline. Short answers and a proposed next step below; I cc'd David (privacy/ops) and Kim (legal) to capture the detail you'll need.

Quick summary of options we can operationalize:
1) No-training commitment (tiered):
   - Service-level exclusion: customer data is not used for model improvement outside the customer tenant.
   - Operational enforcement: request routing to segregated inference pools, KV/prefix caching disabled for opt-out traffic, no adaptive update pipelines run on opt-out buckets.
2) Residency/export lanes:
   - Onshore KMS option + dedicated SFTP export lane for forensic/escrow snapshots (monthly or on-demand).
   - If onshore KMS cannot be provisioned in a region, we offer an "escrow fallback": timely export of artifact snapshots to a mutually agreed SFTP + attestations from our subprocessor chain.
3) Subprocessors & evidence:
   - We will provide a current subprocessor list and a one-time evidence package: attestations + export manifest + ops runbook excerpt (ops_evidence_kms_map.xlsx) for your security team.

Cost implications: there is an incremental cost for dedicated onshore KMS and reserved routing — Marissa will follow up with a delta estimate.

Next step: Marissa, can we propose Tue 4/24 2pm PT for a short sync (20 min)? David / Kim, can you prepare a 1-page ops note and a suggested DPA addendum clause we can share with HealthGrid ahead of the call?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

---
Sean Gallagher
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: ops_evidence_kms_map.xlsx

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Sophia Ramos <sophia.ramos@healthgrid.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-21T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redline (training opt-out + export lanes) — ops detail

Hi Sophia — quick ops addendum from the privacy/infra side. I'm attaching the short checklist we typically provide during procurement reviews. High level:

- Definition: "No-training / no-improve" = no customer inputs (prompts, uploads, session contexts) are routed into any model update or continual learning pipeline. This includes both center-of-train offline datasets and online adaptive update paths.
- Enforcement controls we will implement (for HG opt-out tenants):
  * Tenant routing: traffic tagged at the API layer as HG-optout and routed to segregated inference pools with configuration flags (no-kv-cache, ephemeral-only session storage).
  * KV/Prefix caching: disabled for opt-out traffic to avoid persistent cache leakage into training datasets.
  * Telemetry/telemetry retention: request telemetry is limited to routing metadata and short-lived traces; raw prompts are redacted unless explicitly required for debugging (with customer consent and a documented process).
  * Subprocessor chain: we will provide the list and execute subprocessor attestations; subprocessors must not use HG data for model improvement and must provide signed attestation.
- Evidence package we can deliver within 5 business days after redline sign-off: subprocessor spreadsheet, SFTP export manifest sample, operational runbook excerpt, and a signed attestation from our infra subprocessor.
- Escrow fallback: operational flow is: 1) attempt onshore KMS provisioning; 2) if not feasible, generate per-customer encrypted snapshot (SFTP) and chain-of-custody manifest; 3) provide signed attestation + delivery confirmation. SLA for snapshot delivery is configurable (standard is 5 business days).

Open questions for you:
1) Is the snapshot cadence monthly or on-demand sufficient?
2) Do you require independent third-party verification of the snapshot process (we can enable SOC/3rd-party attestation for an additional cost)?

Happy to walk through this on the call.

-David
David Kim
Senior Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sophia Ramos <sophia.ramos@healthgrid.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: 2028-04-25T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthGrid DPA redline — suggested addendum language

Sophia / team — attaching a proposed short addendum we recommend for the DPA that operationalizes the no-training commitment and escrow fallback. Below is the extract we'd like in the addendum; happy to iterate if you prefer alternate wording.

--- Proposed DPA Addendum (excerpt) ---
1. Definitions: "No-Training Data" means Customer Data that Provider shall not use to improve, fine-tune, or retrain any machine learning models, whether directly or indirectly.
2. Operational Controls: Provider shall implement tenant-level routing and configuration to ensure No-Training Data is processed in segregated inference pools with caching disabled. Provider shall maintain an auditable evidence package (subprocessor list, attestations, export manifest) and deliver the package within five (5) business days upon reasonable request following execution of this Addendum.
3. Escrow Fallback: If Provider cannot provision onshore KMS or otherwise meet residency requirements within thirty (30) calendar days of Customer's written request, Provider shall produce an encrypted snapshot of No-Training Data and deliver it to Customer via SFTP along with a signed chain-of-custody manifest within five (5) business days. The parties may agree in writing to alternative timelines for production and verification.
4. Subprocessors: Provider will maintain a list of subprocessors and secure signed attestations preventing use of No-Training Data for model improvement. Provider will notify Customer of material subprocessor changes thirty (30) days in advance.
---

If that language is acceptable in principle, we'll prepare a tracked addendum to merge into your redline and route for DocuSign. Sean / Marissa: please confirm if Redwood will push the DocuSign envelope and if Marissa can include the cost delta in the draft.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Sophia / HealthGrid procurement — thanks everyone for the quick turn. Quick recap and action items: 

1) Evidence package: David will deliver the subprocessor list + ops runbook excerpt + SFTP manifest sample by EOD 2028-05-03 (5 business days after sign-off). (owner: david_kim)
2) Pricing delta: Marissa to send a ballpark for onshore KMS + reserved routing by 2028-05-01; if HealthGrid wants dedicated capacity we can provide a firm quote within 3 business days thereafter. (owner: marissa_cole)
3) SLA question: no-training tenant routing is configured to preserve latency SLAs; however, large reserved routing commitments may change burst capacity economics. Sean will include a short latency impact note in the quote. (owner: sean_gallagher)
4) DocuSign and redline: Kim will prepare the tracked addendum and Marissa will attach the pricing delta; Redwood will push the DocuSign envelope when HG confirms the two-week review window. Target DocuSign send date: 2028-05-05 (owner: kimberly_park / marissa_cole).

If that aligns, Sophia — can you confirm the two-week review window and whether you prefer monthly snapshots (default) or on-demand exports for the escrow fallback? Once we get that, we'll route the addendum + envelope.

Thanks,
Sean
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
